C ONCLUSIONS AND O PEN P ROBLEMS In this paper, we design the first dynamic deterministic constant-approximate distance oracles with n worst-case update time, and along the way, we develop a few algorithmic tools that may be of independent interest, including local length-constrained flows, dynamic routers, dynamic length-constrained expander decompositions, dynamic lengthreducing emulators and dynamic vertex sparsifiers for distances. Below, we list a few interesting open problems. 1) Optimal approximation-time trade-off: Our approximation ratio of O(exp(poly(1/))) seems far from being optimal. For example, the decremental algorithm against an oblivious adversary by Chechik [8] has (2 + )k − 1)-approximation with O(n1/k+o(1) ) amortized update time. It is a challenging open problem to match this trade-off with algorithms against an adaptive adversary, even in the decremental and amortized setting. Getting poly(1/)-approximation in n update time is already very interesting. 2) Dynamic strong expander decomposition: We only show how to maintain length-constrained expander decomposition in a weak sense. That is, as shown in Theorem 3, we maintain a moving cut C such that any reasonable demand in G − C can be routed in the original graph G with small length and congestion, while a strong decomposition requires that reasonable demands in G − C can be routed in G − C. Can one show a dynamic algorithm for maintaining strong lengthconstrained expander decomposition? In the non-lengthconstrained setting, a near-linear time weak expander decomposition algorithm was also developed first [77] and was later improved to strong expander decomposition [39]. 3) Dynamic vertex sparsifier with worst-case update time: Our dynamic vertex sparsifiers preserving distances with constant approximation (Theorem 6) have amortized update time because the standard reduction from the online-batch dynamic setting to the fully dynamic setting does not work directly when maintaining an explicit object. Hence, it is still an open problem to obtain a deterministic fully dynamic vertex sparsifier for distances with constant approximation and n worst-case 2041 update time. We note that Kyng, Meierhans and Probst Gutenberg [33] have shown dynamic vertex sparsifiers preserving distances with worst-case update time, while their sparsifiers have no(1) approximation and no(1) update time. 4) Local length-constrained (1 + )-approximate maximum flow: As shown in Theorem 2, we localize the approximate length-constrained maxflow algorithm by Haeupler, Hershkowitz and Saranurak [42]. However, our local algorithm only achieves (2 + )-approximation instead of (1 + )-approximation as in [42]. The bottleneck is localizing the approximate lightest path blockers algorithm, a key intermediate step in [42]. It will be interesting to get a (1 + )-approximate local lengthconstrained maxflow algorithm.
